transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Thanks for checking in. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month, so keep it gentle to begin with.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thank you for that information. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good news – it's safe to continue using your eye gel for dry eyes. If you were using it before your operation, you can keep using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running low on it, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know, thank you. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. 

Are you experiencing severe pain, or is it just mild sensitivity?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's just mild sensitivity, nothing severe. Thanks for the advice on sunglasses. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? That would help me give you better advice about what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about ten days since the surgery. The blurriness seems to be improving but slowly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That sounds reassuring that it's improving. At ten days, some blurriness is still quite normal and should continue to improve over time. Just keep an eye on it.

However, if your vision gets significantly worse or stays very blurry, let us know so we can check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you for answering my questions, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm – have all your questions about your surgery and recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and remember to wear those sunglasses outside. All the best with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside." The `escalation_criteria` was also conveyed in the same turn: "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further." All points were covered.
